The Van Allen belts consist of charged particles - protons and electrons - captured by Earth's magnetic field. They do not consist of photonic radiation or neutron radiation, neither of which are captured by magnetic fields. A charged particle passing through a magnetic field experiences an acceleration, trapping it into an orbit - non-charged particles pass straight through magnetic fields. Particle radiation is easily shielded against using non-conductive materials, and require very light shielding. Modern particle radiation shields use plastics like acrylic or polyethylene. Using lead to shield against particle radiation would be counter productive, because when high energy particles strike a metallic target, they create secondary x-rays, called Bremsstrahlung. It likely would take a large thickness of lead to block particle radiation, because it would have to block all of the secondary radiation created by the impact - but nuclear engineering was a developed field by this point, so no-one would have been stupid enough to use lead.

As for "muh dust" below, in a vacuum dust accelerated by the engine would not be decelerated by air resistance, and would only be effected by gravity. Dust clouds are created by the dust kicked up interacting with the air. In other words, it would either fly out and clear the landing area, or it would simply drop back to the surface.
